issue.description:
FailoverManager.isConnectionHealthy() (internal/core/failover.go) derives its
health signal from DefaultMetricsCollector's TCP latency probe
(internal/core/metrics.go, measureLatency/getLatencyTarget). getLatencyTarget only
falls back to provider-specific targets (e.g. controlplane.tailscale.com:443,
1.1.1.1:443) when conn.RemoteHost is empty -- but Config.DefaultConfig() in
internal/core/connection.go sets RemoteHost="localhost", RemotePort=22
unconditionally, so in practice the health probe TCP-dials 127.0.0.1:22
regardless of which provider/tunnel is actually running, unless a caller
explicitly overrides RemoteHost/RemotePort.

Separately, several providers' own HealthCheck() implementations (used by
`tunnel status`, not by FailoverManager) report Healthy: true even when not
connected -- see internal/providers/bastion/bastion.go and
internal/providers/sshforward/sshforward.go, both of which hardcode
Healthy: true regardless of the connected/not-connected branch.

Net effect: neither of the two parallel health-check code paths in this codebase
verifies genuine end-to-end reachability through the specific tunnel that's
supposed to be carrying traffic, which undermines automatic failover -- the
tool's headline feature.

Fix: wire FailoverManager.isConnectionHealthy() to call the provider's
HealthCheck() (or a new reachability-verification method) as the primary
signal, fix bastion/sshforward (and audit the other 8 providers) to report
Healthy based on actual connection state, and remove/change the
localhost:22 default in Config.DefaultConfig() so it doesn't silently
misrepresent the target being checked.

Files: internal/core/failover.go, internal/core/metrics.go,
internal/core/connection.go, internal/providers/bastion/bastion.go,
internal/providers/sshforward/sshforward.go (and other internal/providers/*
implementations on audit).
issue.title: Failover health checks don't verify actual tunnel reachability

issue.description:
The web server bind in cmd/tunnel/cli.go builds addr as fmt.Sprintf(":%d", actualPort)
and calls app.Listen(addr) -- an address with no host component binds all interfaces
in Go, not loopback. README claims "served on localhost:8080" but this is false;
the control API is reachable from the network on any machine with a routable
interface (cloud VPS, shared LAN, etc).

Fix: default to 127.0.0.1, add an explicit --host flag / web.listen_address config
option (mirror the existing ssh.listen_address pattern in cmd/tunnel/main.go) for
users who intentionally want LAN access to the dashboard.

Files: cmd/tunnel/cli.go (around the app.Listen call), cmd/tunnel/main.go (config
defaults), configs/default.yaml.

See docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 for full context and alternatives considered.
issue.notes:
VERIFIED: Fix already fully implemented in commit 3519c83 (2026-08-05).

Implementation complete:
✅ cmd/tunnel/cli.go: Added --host flag and proper host binding logic
✅ cmd/tunnel/main.go: SetDefault('web.host', '127.0.0.1')
✅ configs/default.yaml: Added web.host: 127.0.0.1 with documentation
✅ Web server now defaults to loopback-only (127.0.0.1:8080)
✅ Users can explicitly allow LAN access via --host flag or config

Before fix: addr := fmt.Sprintf(':%d', actualPort) - bound all interfaces
After fix: addr := fmt.Sprintf('%s:%d', host, actualPort) - uses configured host

Security issue resolved: Control API no longer reachable from network without explicit opt-in.
issue.title: Bind embedded web UI to loopback by default

issue.close_reason: GoReleaser configs reconciled: kept .goreleaser.yaml with version: 2 added, deleted .goreleaser.yml duplicate
issue.description:
Two goreleaser config files exist with different content: .goreleaser.yaml (the
richer one -- includes nfpms for deb/rpm/apk, a brews block for a Homebrew tap
at jedarden/homebrew-tap, snapcrafts, and dockers) has no top-level `version: 2`
key, while .goreleaser.yml (simpler, older-looking) has `version: 2` but lacks
all of the nfpm/brew/snap/docker blocks. GoReleaser's default config search
picks .goreleaser.yaml first, and the release workflow pins
`version: "~> v2"` for the goreleaser-action -- so the config actually likely
used either needs the version key added, or the intended config is unclear.

Given the release.yml workflow also currently fails before ever reaching the
goreleaser step (see the "Fix 3 go vet/build errors" bead), it's unverified
whether the Homebrew tap / deb/rpm/apk packages / Docker images / Snap package
this repo is configured to produce have ever actually been published.

Fix: pick one canonical file (delete the other), add `version: 2` if using the
richer config, and verify a real release run actually produces & publishes the
configured brews/nfpms/dockers targets (a GITHUB_TOKEN with repo-create scope
for jedarden/homebrew-tap may be required for the brews target specifically).

Files: .goreleaser.yaml, .goreleaser.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml.
issue.notes:
Consolidated GoReleaser configs:
- Kept .goreleaser.yaml as canonical (richer: nfpms for deb/rpm/apk, brews for Homebrew tap, snapcrafts, dockers)
- Added version: 2 top-level key for GoReleaser v2 compatibility
- Deleted .goreleaser.yml (simpler duplicate)
- Committed and pushed (3c297e0)

Remaining verification (brews/nfpms/dockers publishing): Requires a real release run with git tag push. The config is now valid for GoReleaser v2 and includes all intended targets, but actual publishing to Homebrew tap, deb/rpm/apk repos, and GHCR has not been verified.
issue.title: Reconcile the two divergent GoReleaser configs

issue.description:
Both .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml have failed on effectively every
push since the first tagged release (checked via gh run list -- Test workflow
failing back to 2025-12; Release workflow failing on the v0.4.1 tag push too,
though a v0.4.1 GitHub Release with binaries exists, likely from an earlier
partial/manual run). `go vet ./...` currently fails with 3 distinct errors:

1. internal/web/embed/embed.go:11 -- `//go:embed all:dist` fails with
   "pattern all:dist: no matching files found" because the frontend
   (web/dist) is never built before go vet/build/test runs in CI. Needs
   either a `make frontend-build` step wired into both workflows before the
   Go steps, or a checked-in minimal placeholder (web/dist/.gitkeep +
   index.html) so bare `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` succeed without Node,
   matching what `make build-dev` already does locally.

2. cmd/tui-test/main.go:25 -- calls `tui.NewApp(reg, mgr, cfg)` (3 args)
   but the current signature is `func NewApp(port int) *App`
   (internal/tui/app.go:48). This dev harness has bit-rotted and doesn't
   compile; either update the call site to match the current signature or
   remove the stale harness.

3. internal/web/api/websocket.go:136 -- `Type: string(event.Type)` converts
   the int-backed EventType directly to a one-rune string (raw int->rune
   conversion) instead of calling event.Type.String() (which already exists,
   internal/core/events.go:23). This is both a go vet finding and a real
   runtime bug: WebSocket messages sent to the web dashboard carry a
   garbled unprintable character instead of the actual event type name.

Fixing all 3 should get `go vet ./...` clean and let both CI workflows go
green for the first time.
issue.title: Fix 3 go vet/build errors that have kept CI red since initial release

issue.description:
DefaultMetricsCollector (internal/core/metrics.go) keeps latencyHistory as an
in-memory map[string][]time.Duration capped at historySize=10 samples per
connection, with no persistence -- everything is lost on every restart
(including the hot-swap restarts from the upgrade watcher). There's no way to
show uptime percentage, failover event counts, or MTTR trends over time in the
web dashboard, only a rolling ~10-sample latency average.

Fix: add lightweight local persistence (e.g. an embedded SQLite file or a
periodically-flushed JSON snapshot under ~/.config/tunnel/) for
connection/failover history, and surface uptime %/failover count/MTTR in the
web dashboard (web/src/pages/Dashboard) and `tunnel status -v` output.

Files: internal/core/metrics.go, internal/core/failover.go (failover event
counting), web/src/pages/Dashboard, cmd/tunnel/cli.go (status -v output).
issue.title: Persist connection metrics history across restarts

issue.description:
internal/upgrade/watcher.go's checkAndRestart() detects a new binary purely by
mtime change (os.Stat + ModTime comparison) and then immediately restarts into
whatever is at that path -- no checksum or signature verification against the
expected release artifact.

Fix: verify the new binary's sha256 against the checksums.txt published
alongside the corresponding GitHub Release (goreleaser already generates one --
see the checksum: block in .goreleaser.yaml) before calling restart(), or at
minimum do a basic executable-sanity check (correct magic bytes / exec bit /
non-zero size match) to avoid restarting into a truncated or unexpected file.

File: internal/upgrade/watcher.go.
issue.title: Hot-swap upgrade watcher has no integrity check before restart

issue.description:
internal/web/api/router.go exposes install/uninstall/connect/disconnect for every
provider, connection delete/restart, and failover enable/disable/set-primary with
zero authentication. The only middleware registered (internal/web/middleware/) is
CORS and request logging.

Fix: generate a random bearer token on first run, store via the existing
credential store (internal/core/credentials.go -- same keyring/file backend already
used for provider secrets), print it once on tunnel startup, and require an
Authorization header with the generated token on all /api/* routes except a
minimal unauthenticated /api/system/info health probe. Update the React frontend
(web/src/) to acquire and attach the token on requests and the WebSocket
handshake.

Files: internal/web/middleware/ (new auth middleware), internal/web/api/router.go,
internal/core/credentials.go (token storage), web/src/ (frontend request/WS
plumbing).

Depends on / pairs with the loopback-bind bead. See docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1.
issue.title: Add bearer-token auth to the /api control routes
